title: Boids: Three Rules, One Flock
description: Separation, alignment and cohesion are the only three rules. The shape of the flock follows from them. Ten presets, 2D and 3D, with predators, obstacles and currents you can paint into the sky.

title: Hare & Lynx: Predator and Prey Cycles
description: Every dot is one animal with its own energy budget, grazing, hunting and breeding. The boom and bust population cycles come out of those individual decisions.

title: Conway's Game of Life
description: One rule about live and dead neighbours is enough to produce gliders, oscillators and patterns that never settle down.

title: Traffic Jams
description: Jams form on an open road with no obstacle and no accident. All it takes is drivers reacting to the car in front.

title: Schelling's Segregation Model
description: Mild individual preferences about who lives next door are enough to segregate a whole city. A classic result in social science.

title: Double Pendulum: Chaos
description: Release a hundred pendulums that differ by a tenth of a degree and watch them tear apart. The clearest demonstration that deterministic and predictable are not the same thing.

title: Epidemic Spread (SIR)
description: Susceptible, infected and recovered agents wander and mix. Change the infection rate and the recovery time to make an outbreak burn out or take off.

title: Lorenz Attractor
description: The first picture of chaos anyone plotted. Turn the heating up past 24.7 and a system that used to settle down never settles again. Rotate it, and release a swarm to watch identical starts come apart.

title: N-Body Gravity
description: Newton's one rule, applied to everything at once. Set up a star system, a binary pair or a collapsing cloud, then sling new bodies in and watch orbits form and merge.

title: Reaction-Diffusion
description: Two chemicals spread and react by the Gray-Scott rules. Spots, stripes and coral shapes appear on their own. Pick a preset or paint your own seed.

title: Pharmacokinetics
description: How the concentration of a drug in the body rises and falls over time, and what different dosing schedules do to that curve.
